teaser: Tiny teeth, one slider, and a neat click together.
title: A zipper clicks together.
question: How can one slider join two rows of tiny teeth?
idea: A Y-shaped path inside the slider guides two rows together so the zipper teeth can interlock, one after another.

curiosity.intro: Start with a question. Look closely at the boundary where open becomes closed.

questions.question: What changes right where the slider sits?
questions.notice: Below the slider are two separate rows. Above it is one joined row.
questions.say: The slider does not glue the sides. It guides matching zipper teeth into an interlocking pattern.
questions.try: Trace each open row toward the slider, then follow the single closed row away from it.

questions.question: Why are zipper teeth shaped with bumps and pockets?
questions.notice: A bump on one side settles into a pocket on the other side.
questions.say: Alternating teeth nest across the gap. Their shapes help the two rows hold together.
questions.try: Point to one left tooth, then the right tooth that fits beside it.

questions.question: What path is hiding inside the slider?
questions.notice: Two wide channels curve toward one narrow opening, like the arms of a Y.
questions.say: The slider's Y-shaped channel bends both rows inward in the right order.
questions.try: Draw a Y in the air. Bring two fingertips down its arms and out together.

questions.question: How can the same slider open the zipper again?
questions.notice: Moving the other way sends the joined row toward the fork in the channel.
questions.say: The center wedge guides the interlocked teeth apart and sends each row out a different side.
questions.try: Trace the joined row toward the fork, then split your fingers along two paths.

plates.title: Where open becomes closed
plates.alt: Big and Little Wonderer study a half-closed zipper on a canvas pouch. Two open tooth rows enter the slider and one joined row leaves it.
plates.caption: A close imagined view. The zipper is enlarged to help us see.

plates.title: Bumps fit pockets
plates.alt: An enlarged zipper shows alternating teeth, each with a rounded bump nested into a pocket across the center line.
plates.caption: Zipper elements are enlarged and simplified so their nesting shapes are clear.

plates.title: A Y inside the slider
plates.alt: A cutaway zipper slider reveals two curved channels meeting at one narrow exit around a central wedge.
plates.caption: A cutaway explanation of the hidden channel, enlarged and simplified.

plates.title: One pair after another
plates.alt: The slider moves along two zipper tapes while successive teeth from alternating sides settle into a single interlocked row.
plates.caption: The pictured motion is slowed into one clear moment.

plates.title: The path works backward
plates.alt: A close cutaway shows a joined zipper row meeting the slider's center wedge and leaving as two separate rows.

plates.title: A neat stop at the top

reading.title: Follow the slider
reading.coverText: Two tooth rows enter. One joined row comes out.
reading.foldableTitle: A little book of tiny teeth
reading.foldableNote: Follow two rows through one hidden path.
reading.parentNote: Age 8. Welcome spoken answers and dictation. Use an intact zipper only, and keep fingers and loose fabric away from the moving slider.

beats.title: A boundary that moves
beats.passage: Little Wonderer found the place where the pouch changed. Below the slider, two rows of zipper teeth stood apart. Above it, they made one joined row. The boundary moved whenever the slider moved. “So the slider must be doing something inside,” Little said.
beats.prompt: What evidence shows that the slider changes the two rows?

foldable.heading: A moving boundary
foldable.body: Below the slider, two tooth rows stood apart. Above it, they made one joined row. Little wondered what happened inside.

beats.title: A bump and a pocket
beats.passage: Up close, each zipper tooth was really a shaped element. A rounded bump on one element fitted into a pocket on the other side. The elements alternated left, right, left, right. Interlock means to fit together so connected shapes hold one another in place.
beats.prompt: How does an alternating pattern help the elements interlock?

foldable.heading: Bump meets pocket
foldable.body: Each zipper element had a bump and a pocket. Left and right elements alternated, nesting across the middle to hold together.

beats.title: A hidden Y-shaped path
beats.passage: The cutaway revealed a channel shaped like the letter Y. Two wide paths curved around a center wedge, then met at one narrow path. As the slider traveled upward, its angled walls nudged both tooth rows inward. The slider was a moving guide, not a row of teeth itself.
beats.prompt: Why does the channel need two entrances and one exit to close the zipper?

foldable.heading: A hidden Y path
foldable.body: Inside the slider, two channels curved around a center wedge and met. Angled walls guided both tooth rows inward.

beats.title: One click after another
beats.passage: Little followed the slider slowly. Its channel lined up one element from the left, then one from the right. Bump met pocket. The next pair followed. Many tiny interlocks formed one flexible zipper chain behind the slider. The slider did not pull the teeth straight across; it curved them into place.
beats.prompt: How does the curved path make closing different from pulling the rows straight together?

foldable.heading: One after another
foldable.body: The channel lined up left and right elements. Bump met pocket, then the next pair followed. A flexible zipper chain formed behind the slider.

beats.title: The wedge separates
beats.passage: Then Little moved the slider back. The joined row entered the narrow end. Inside, the center wedge steered one side left and the other side right. The bumps slipped out of their pockets along the curved paths. The same Y-shaped channel worked in reverse to open the pouch.
beats.prompt: What changes when the joined row meets the center wedge?

foldable.heading: The wedge separates
foldable.body: Moving back sent the joined row toward the center wedge. It guided one side left and the other right, opening the zipper.

beats.title: Click at the stop
beats.passage: Little closed the pouch once more. The last elements nested, and the slider met the top stop with a neat click. The stop kept it from sliding off the teeth. Two rows had become one strong, bendable seam. Little looked at a jacket zipper. “Is the same hidden Y inside that one too?”
beats.prompt: Why are both the shaped elements and the top stop needed?

foldable.heading: Click at the stop
foldable.body: The last elements nested. The slider clicked against the top stop, which kept it from running off the closed row.

math.title: Compare the tooth rows
math.intro: Use these pretend zipper-design counts. Compare each pair or round one count to the nearest ten.

tasks.prompt: One sample zipper has 38 elements along a pocket. Another has 46. Put >, <, or = in the circle. Which is the greater count?
tasks.hint: Compare the tens first. If the tens match, compare the ones.
tasks.worked: 38 < 46. 4 tens are more than 3 tens, so the greater count is 46.
tasks.label: TASK 1

tasks.prompt: A long bag zipper has 72 elements. A short pouch zipper has 27. Put >, <, or = in the circle. Which is the greater count?
tasks.hint: Look at the tens digits before the ones digits.
tasks.worked: 72 > 27. 7 tens are more than 2 tens, so the greater count is 72.
tasks.label: TASK 2

tasks.prompt: A zipper design gives the left tape 54 elements and the right tape 54 elements. Put >, <, or = in the circle. What shared count do the matching rows have?
tasks.hint: When both tens and ones match, use the equal sign.
tasks.worked: 54 = 54. Both rows have the shared count 54.
tasks.label: TASK 3

tasks.prompt: A design note lists 43 zipper elements. What is 43 rounded to the nearest ten?
tasks.hint: 43 lies between 40 and 50. Look at the ones digit.
tasks.worked: 43 has 3 ones, so it rounds down to 40.
tasks.label: TASK 4

tasks.prompt: Another zipper design lists 67 elements. What is 67 rounded to the nearest ten?
tasks.hint: 67 lies between 60 and 70. A ones digit of 5 or more rounds up.
tasks.worked: 67 has 7 ones, so it rounds up to 70.
tasks.label: TASK 5

tasks.prompt: A long zipper design lists 95 elements. What is 95 rounded to the nearest ten?
tasks.hint: A ones digit of exactly 5 rounds up to the next ten.
tasks.worked: 95 has 5 ones, so it rounds up to 100.
tasks.label: TASK 6

math.extension: Choose two zipper counts in your home. Estimate by rounding each count to the nearest ten; do not count teeth while a zipper is moving.
math.printNote: Use the printed counts. The illustrations are not exact data.
math.parentNote: Grade 2 math. The six tasks include comparison with <, >, and = plus nearest-ten rounding, including the 5-rounds-up rule. All counts are invented for the math story.
math.answerKeyIntro: Grade 2 math. Compare tens before ones. For rounding, 0–4 rounds down and 5–9 rounds up.

writing.title: Give the mechanism your words.
writing.intro: Choose a scene. Look, say an idea, then draw or write.
writing.draw: Draw the slider's Y-shaped path. Add arrows to show two rows becoming one.

frames.hint: what is separate and what is joined?
how do the bumps and pockets fit?
what does the Y-shaped channel guide?

writing.check: Read your words aloud. Did you connect a shape to its job with because, so, or however?
writing.parentNote: About 15 min. Accept invented spelling, speech, dictation, or a labeled drawing. One clear cause-and-effect idea is enough.

answers.label: Reading · 1
answers.text: Below the slider the rows are separate; above it they are joined. The boundary moves with the slider, showing that it guides the change.

answers.label: Reading · 2
answers.text: Closing sends separate rows through two channels toward one exit. Opening sends one joined row toward the center wedge and out through two channels.

answers.label: Reading · 3
answers.text: Each element locks with its neighbors at the center, but the many small connections and fabric tapes can still bend as a chain.

answers.label: Writing
answers.text: A spoken, dictated, drawn, or written explanation counts. Example: “The Y-shaped channel guides two tooth rows into one interlocked row.”

parentGuidance: Use a clean, intact zipper on a pouch or jacket. Move it slowly while keeping fingers, hair, and loose fabric away from the slider. Do not take a slider apart or handle broken metal teeth. Zipper types differ: this pack shows an enlarged, simplified molded-tooth zipper. The teeth are more precisely called elements. A slider has internal guide channels and a central post or wedge; moving one way brings the rows into interlocking engagement, while moving the other way separates them. Stops keep the slider from leaving the chain. Some sliders also have a small locking part, but that extra mechanism is outside this lesson.

why: Following one slider along the teeth helps your child connect a Y-shaped path to how two rows of tiny teeth lock into one smooth line.
